title: High-power hybrid commutated converter for carbon-neutral power transmission
abstract:
Nature Communications, Published online: 22 July 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-75691-5

The study presents a high-power hybrid commutated converter system that combines forced and recovery-enhanced commutation to enable reliable, efficient long-distance transmission of renewable energy, validated at 120 kV/360 MW in real-world projects.

title: Minute-scale red phosphorescence in carbon nanodots
abstract:
Nature Communications, Published online: 22 July 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-76003-7

The authors design carbon nanodots with minute-scale red phosphorescence through combination of excited-state engineering and machine learning optimization, opening opportunities for low-energy optoelectronic devices.

title: Comparative regulomics of wood formation across dicot and conifer trees
abstract:
Nature Communications, Published online: 22 July 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-75624-2

Understanding how wood formation is regulated could help improve biomass production and carbon sequestration in trees. Here the authors report the activity of genes underlying wood formation in six diverse tree species revealing shared and lineage-specific regulatory programs.

title: Association-gated multiphoton activation of inert haloarenes via sequential electron donor–acceptor assembly
abstract:
Nature Communications, Published online: 22 July 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-75858-0

Extreme photoreduction is often limited by uncontrolled, diffusion-driven reactivity of highly energetic intermediates. Here, the authors report an association-gated photocatalytic strategy that assembles sequential donor–acceptor complexes to create confined reaction pockets, enabling selective activation of strong carbon–halogen bonds.

title: Kinetically templated fibrillar self-assembly via two-dimensional nanocrystals enables 21% efficient organic solar cells
abstract:
Nature Communications, Published online: 22 July 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-75699-x

Controlling long-range, directional fibrillar morphology is important for organic solar cells (OSC). Here, the authors show that cobalt phosphosulfide nanocrystals can template film formation in OSCs, improving charge generation and transport, and achieving a power conversion efficiency of 21.0%.

title: The bacterial mechanosensitive channel MscM gates through concerted changes in its transmembrane and cytoplasmic domains
abstract:
Nature Communications, Published online: 22 July 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-75798-9

Mechanosensitive channels in bacteria provide protection against hypoosmotic shock. Here, the authors use cryo-electron microscopy to reveal the gating mechanism of MscS-like channel EcMscM, showing that the conformations of the transmembrane and cytoplasmic domains are coupled.

title: Modeling network evolution by multi-agent reinforcement learning
abstract:
Nature Communications, Published online: 21 July 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-75382-1

This paper introduces NEMARL, a multi-agent reinforcement learning framework for network evolution that models node-level decision making and coordination. The approach reproduces key network properties, fits real-world data, and demonstrates effectiveness across multiple scenario tests.

title: Catalytic electrophilic arene C–H chlorination by rethinking the century-old willgerodt reagent
abstract:
Nature Communications, Published online: 21 July 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-75774-3

Authors synthesize a variant of a decades-old chlorinating reagent and show its competence in catalytic electrophilic arene C–H chlorination.
